summary: Configured node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain seven compressed rotations, and preserve writes across rotation with copytruncate. Verified live rotation behavior and persistence through a node reboot.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Validated the policy and forced a real rotation while a writer retained an open file descriptor.
Confirmed the pre-rotation content was compressed and the same writer added post-rotation content to the active log.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed and the configuration, logs, archive, timer, and system health recovered.

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed policy specifies daily, rotate 7, and compress; forced rotation created app.log.1.gz; the global logrotate configuration recognizes the policy and the daily timer is scheduled.

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A writer opened the log before rotation and retained its descriptor. Its pre-rotation marker appeared in the compressed archive, while its post-rotation marker appeared in the active log.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID e65e6bcf-e09d-42b7-8317-cb6310086cb7, received safe reboot acknowledgement, observed changed boot ID fc8361f8-d3c5-4831-b634-288a8e19f16e, and verified the system was running with the timer active, policy intact, active log preserved, and compressed archive healthy.
